modernized_recommendation.status: OWNER-RESOLVED PHYSICAL BMC UART CONSOLE TEST
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Attach the scope ruling to evidence of connector/pinout/voltage, console ownership, terminal parameters, redacted live identity, marker bytes in both directions, physical/session start/end and no-damage/no-state-change verification.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Separates physical UART from logical SOL until the platform proves their relationship and adds electrical and interaction safety controls.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A sensor read or even a successful UART attachment cannot prove the stated SOL/ttyS0 criterion unless routing is explicitly established.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Incorrect voltage or pinout can damage hardware immediately; interactive BMC console input can also change privileged configuration, so visual and physical controls remain essential.

project_override_considerations: The Project must decide whether Criteria's SOL/ttyS0 wording is a copied defect, describes the same physical BMC console through a platform-specific bridge, or requires a separate checkpoint. The later duplicate-code variant remains independent.

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items and Procedure require a physical dongle on the BMC console, while Criteria requires SOL on ttyS0. These may be distinct endpoints and evidence paths; platform equivalence cannot be assumed.

blocked_analysis.analysis: An owner scope ruling and vendor wiring/routing documents are normal project inputs. Execution becomes BLOCKED if the authoritative console endpoint or safe electrical contract cannot be established.

engineering_decision_request.question: Resolve whether Functionality row 1672 validates the physical BMC-console UART dongle path stated by Items/Procedure, SOL on ttyS0 at 115200 stated by Criteria, a documented platform bridge proving they are the same endpoint, or separately accepted checkpoints; define authoritative connector/routing, console owner and evidence while preserving Master.

review_improvement: Exposes the physical-UART versus SOL/ttyS0 mismatch before anyone guesses wiring or accepts unrelated sensor evidence, while retaining the manual text-fidelity objective.
independent_technical_reasoning: Electrical UART identity and logical terminal identity are separate facts. A dongle can produce readable output from the wrong header, and SOL can route a different UART than the physical BMC console. The acceptance route must therefore be owner-defined and independently identified before harmless copy/paste can prove anything about the intended interface.
